newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Cariplo sees higher 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Cariplo sees higher 1996 profit.

text.p: Italy's largest savings bank Cariplo expects to see 1996 results slightly up on those of last year, chairman Sandro Molinari said.
"Our end-year results are in line with 1995, with a slight improvement barring surprises," he told reporters while attending a conference.
Cariplo posted consolidated 1995 net profit of 326 billion lire, a 76.1 percent rise on the previous year.
For the first half of 1996, the Milan-based bank reported group net profit of 189 billion lire, a rise of 26.8 percent on the same 1995 period.

Moody's Investors Service on Monday lowered Cariplo's bank financial strength rating to C+ from B, saying the lower rating reflected the negative impact on the group's financial fundamentals caused by its loss-making south Italian units.
Molinari said he was surprised by the lower rating, both because 1996 forecasts were positive and because "we don't think we should be penalised for the action we are taking in the south of Italy."

Cariplo last week announced it would launch a rescue plan for two southern Italian savings banks which it controls, saying the plan for Caripuglia and Carical would involve an 800 billion lire capital increase.
Moody's decision followed similar long-term outlook downgrades by both S&P and IBCA this summer.
Asked about Cariplo's long-delayed privatisation plans, Molinari said "we are thinking of carrying out the operation in the new year."
Cariplo pulled plans for a partial flotation in the summer of 1994 at the last moment, blaming adverse market conditions.
Molinari also confirmed Cariplo was studying a plan to set up a banking-insurance company with Italian insurer INA.
